channel.title: What NBA players and coaches have said about Jerry Sloan | HoopsMatic
channel.description: The latest quotes about Jerry Sloan from NBA players, coaches and executives, with context and sources.

item.title: Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Chris Webber, John Stockton
item.description:
Karl Malone:

“I love Chris Webber but this was one time where I wanted to kick his ass. Right? So we had been wearing them out – at home – and Chris Webber started at half court looking for John Stockton. On the flip side, I say ‘Good on you Chris for studying the playbook. And we ran that four up and he didn’t even care. He hit Stockton right in the sternum with his elbow. I damn near felt it and [it] hurt. ...I felt so bad I went over to Coach [Jerry] Sloan and I said, ‘Coach, don’t run that again, please.’ Stock[ton] looked at me and said ‘No, I’m good’ and the next play– well, you know.”

Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Chris Webber, John Stockton, Jan 19, 2021. Source: The Players' Tribune.

item.title: Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
That leadership style reminds Williams of someone he used to play for in Utah.

“I honestly see Jerry Sloan in him. Jerry Sloan was the same way,”

Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan, Dec 17, 2020. Source: The Athletic.

item.title: Deron Williams on Carlos Boozer, Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Deron Williams on playing for the legendary Jerry Sloan and his toughness and coaching style:

“Do you know how much dummy offense we did? Man, so we would do it...some days we would come in, and he’d put me at the five and he’d put Booze [Carlos Boozer] at the one. You had to know, he wanted you to know every position so that everything was interchangeable. And that’s how good we run it. That’s what made it so successful, is how hard we ran it and how well we ran it.”

Deron Williams on Carlos Boozer, Jerry Sloan, Dec 8, 2020. Source: The Players' Tribune.

item.title: Gregg Popovich on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Michael C. Wright:Pop on Sloan:

“It’s a sad day for all of us who knew Jerry Sloan. He was genuine & true. That is rare. He was a mentor for me from afar until I got to know him. A man who suffered no fools, he possessed a humor, often disguised, and had a heart as big as the prairie.”

Gregg Popovich on Jerry Sloan, May 22, 2020. Source: Twitter @mikecwright.

item.title: Kenny Smith on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Kenny Smith (@Kenny Smith) thoughts on the late Jerry Sloan:

“The one thing is, we didn’t feel like we were ever playing against @Utah Jazz. We thought we were playing against Jerry Sloan teams, which is a difference. It was a unique style that was so different from every...”

Kenny Smith on Jerry Sloan, May 22, 2020. Source: Twitter @MarkBermanFox26.

item.title: Rudy Tomjanovich on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Mark Berman:Rudy Tomjanovich on the late Jerry Sloan:

“He was a good guy, no nonsense. What you see is what you get. He coached the way he played. His teams reflected his blue-collar mentality. I felt a little bit of a bond with him. I was there in New Orleans (as a #Rockets ass’t, scouting)..”

Rudy Tomjanovich on Jerry Sloan, May 22, 2020. Source: Twitter @MarkBermanFox26.

item.title: Sasha Pavlovic on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
“However,Sloan never showed any arrogance, nor did he show that anything is measured by money. I always remember the pictures of him coming to training in a truck, like the rest of the world.”

Sasha Pavlovic on Jerry Sloan, May 22, 2020. Source: EuroHoops.net.

item.title: DeShawn Stevenson on Jerry Sloan, Karl Malone, John Stockton, John Starks
item.description:
DeShawn Stevenson on his high-school-to-NBA transition:

“Mine was tough. I feel like I had to grind harder. I didn’t get the same chances as most straight-out-of-high-school guys. I went to a team that had been to the Finals two years in a row and was trying to compete for a championship and they had John Stockton, Karl Malone, Byron Russell and John Starks. We had seasoned vets, so I didn’t play that much. Also, I had a coach who was hard-nosed in Jerry Sloan; he didn’t play any games. I came out of high school and was flashy, so it was an adjustment. I kind of got stereotyped… It was tough, man. Sometimes I would get picked on really bad...”

DeShawn Stevenson on Jerry Sloan, Karl Malone, John Stockton, John Starks, Mar 19, 2019. Source: audioBoom.

item.title: Gregg Popovich on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Bill Oram:Gregg Popovich asked what he thinks of Lonzo as a player.

“I haven’t watched him. ... If I have to watch film that’s what assistant coaches are for. Jerry Sloan taught me that.”

Gregg Popovich on Jerry Sloan, Jan 11, 2018. Source: Twitter @billoram.

item.title: Rick Carlisle on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Ryan McDonald:Rick Carlisle:

“Jerry Sloan is one of the all-time ass-kickers in the NBA. I really can't put it any other way.”

Rick Carlisle on Jerry Sloan, Jun 8, 2016. Source: Twitter @ryanwmcdonald.

item.title: Jeff Hornacek on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Nor does it sound like Hornacek has a singular, silver-bullet explanation to how he'll fix New York's problematic defense.

“I played for Cotton Fitzsimmons, who was very offensive-minded, and Jerry Sloan, who is very defensive-minded,”

Jeff Hornacek on Jerry Sloan, Jun 3, 2016. Source: USA Today Sports.

item.title: Kermit Washington on Phil Jackson, Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Former NBA All-Star Kermit Washington joined the Bald Faced Truth radios show (12-3p on 750-AM and 102.9-FM) to talk about his career, Damian Lillard, and why he thinks Jerry Sloan was a better coach than Phil Jackson.

“I think Jerry Sloan is a lot better coach than Phil Jackson,”

Kermit Washington on Phil Jackson, Jerry Sloan, May 18, 2016. Source: Oregonian.

item.title: Quin Snyder on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Andy Larsen:Quin Snyder on Jerry Sloan:

“For me personally, he's been tremendously supportive and positive... A great resource.”

Quin Snyder on Jerry Sloan, Apr 7, 2016. Source: Twitter @andyblarsen.

item.title: Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
“You know, some of those days, I wish I could have controlled them, but I was young, hot-headed and just wanted to win. I'm a lot more mellow now, I think sometimes to a fault. The situation in Utah and how the media reacted kind of took my passion away, my fire away a little bit, because it's like I couldn't be who I was. I got into it with Coach [Sloan] maybe a couple of times. I've seen him get into it with a lot of guys a lot worse, but it happened that he decided to step down after one of our arguments. So of course, it's my fault. It's just something that you've got to live with, you have to take.”

Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan, Nov 30, 2015. Source: ESPN.com.

item.title: Kevon Looney on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Tony Jones:Kevon Looney on his visit:

“I got to shake hands with Jerry Sloan. I grew up watching him on TV”

Kevon Looney on Jerry Sloan, May 15, 2015. Source: Twitter @Tjonessltrib.

item.title: Carlos Boozer on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Carlos Boozer on the Jazz:

“Very athletic group of guys. Well coached. I know Jerry (Sloan) is in the mix somewhere.”

Carlos Boozer on Jerry Sloan, Nov 26, 2013. Source: Twitter @tribjazz.

item.title: Gordon Hayward on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
“Going into the season, I thought if anyone was a staple it would be Coach Sloan and Williams,”

Gordon Hayward on Jerry Sloan, Feb 10, 2012. Source: Yahoo! Sports.

item.title: Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Reached by phone Saturday, Karl Malone was asked whether Sloan lacked support from management that night in the locker room in 2011.

“The only thing I can tell you is that's great. But there's nothing that can be said or done to hurt my relationship with Jerry Sloan,”

Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Feb 5, 2012. Source: Deseret News.

item.title: Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Jody Genessy:Karl Malone told @therockmonster:

“There's nothing that can be said or done to hurt my relationship with Jerry Sloan.”

Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Feb 4, 2012. Source: Twitter.

item.title: Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Greg Miller
item.description:
“… You give a guy that much power, and he’s the kind of player you think he played hard all the time, but if he wanted to sulk he could sulk.… I never went to Larry [Miller] to talk about Coach Sloan. … It’s not one time, in my gut and heart, that I would go over his head.”

Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Greg Miller, Feb 3, 2012. Source: Salt Lake Tribune.

item.title: Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
“I know for a fact that [Sloan] was overridden on practices sometime on the road because Deron was calling our G.M. at that time,”

Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Feb 3, 2012. Source: Salt Lake Tribune.

item.title: Andrei Kirilenko on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Andrei Kirilenko tells HOOPSWORLD.

“We always have Jerry (Sloan) around and he could figure it out easily, but the last three weeks or month have been different. There's no Jerry. What we're trying to do right now is kind of establish ourselves, understand who we are as a team and what condition we're in.”

Andrei Kirilenko on Jerry Sloan, Mar 12, 2011. Source: HoopsWorld.

item.title: Kevin O'Connor on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
O'Connor on Jerry Sloan:

“We were together for almost 12 years, and I’m not sure how many Gms can say that. It’s difficult. It’s a growing process now for Ty, and he’s doing a terrific job with it, but it’s certainly…From a personal standpoint, you always knew that the guy had your back. You always knew it. He didn’t need to tell me it. He just did it. And I hope that he felt the same way about me and that we’re all in this together. It’s not ‘personnel is over here and coaches are over here.’ Maybe because I coached for 12 years and spent time with Larry Brown, it’s all about trying to do it the right way and you’re all doing it.”

Kevin O'Connor on Jerry Sloan, Mar 10, 2011. Source: NBA Confidential.

item.title: Paul Silas on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Paul Silas on On Jerry Sloan’s exit in Utah:

“You’ve got to realize what our league is really about now and it is a player’s league. Once you get into a thing with a player, and they have to make a decision, very rarely are they going to make a decision in favor of the coach. Now, they say that didn’t happen, and that’s a distinct possibility, but Jerry Sloan was one of the all-time great coaches. … I just think he felt the time was right for him to step down and I have to commend him for that.”

Paul Silas on Jerry Sloan, Feb 14, 2011. Source: Sports Radio Interviews.

item.title: Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
“If they want to believe Coach Sloan and Kevin O’Connor and Phil Johnson [the longtime Jazz assistant coach who also resigned Thursday] and me, then they can believe that. “It frustrates me because, you know, I’m not the smartest guy, but I’m also not stupid, and I would never try to force out a Hall of Fame coach – you know, somebody who’s so loved in this community where I’m playing at right now. I’ve been smart. I’ve handled the free-agent talk and all that stuff. So why would I go and do something stupid like that?”

Deron Williams on Jerry Sloan, Feb 12, 2011. Source: Yahoo! Sports.

item.title: Karl Malone on Larry Miller, Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Asked if today's players have too much pull, Malone thought back to his own contentious battles with Sloan over the years.

“I remember [late team owner] Larry Miller in this locker room, right here when me and coach Sloan was butting heads after a game in front of everybody,”

Karl Malone on Larry Miller, Jerry Sloan, Feb 12, 2011. Source: ESPN.com.

item.title: Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
When pressed on it, Malone said,

“What I said is what I said. I know Jerry Sloan. And the people that know him the closest know that man would never resign or quit if you want to, on nothing. I don't care what it is.”

Karl Malone on Jerry Sloan, Feb 12, 2011. Source: CBSSports.com.

item.title: Jerry Krause on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
KC Johnson:Jerry Krause on Sloan:

“Jerry is one of the greatest competitors I’ve ever seen, on par with MJ. There will never be another like him.”

Jerry Krause on Jerry Sloan, Feb 11, 2011. Source: Twitter.

item.title: Doc Rivers on Jerry Sloan
item.description:
Adrian Wojnarowski:Doc Rivers on Jerry Sloan:

“He's been like a rock --- and all of a sudden the rock is gone.”

Doc Rivers on Jerry Sloan, Feb 10, 2011. Source: Twitter.
